newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bosnian Serb to go on Swiss trial for war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb to go on Swiss trial for war crimes.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb man accused of torture and killing during the Bosnian war will stand trial in a Swiss military court next week in the country's first Yugoslav war crimes trial, a military justice official said on Thursday.

Sergeant Jurg van Wijnkoop said the 32-year-old man had been accused by witnesses of having tortured prisoners and killed one person in the Serb-run detention camps of Keretrem and Omarska in northwest Bosnia in 1992 during the war in former Yugoslavia.

The unidentified man, held in a Swiss military prison since his arrest in April 1995 in Geneva where he was an asylum seeker, denies all the charges and claims he was in Germany and Austria at the time, Wijnkoop said.
The U.N. war crimes tribunal for former Yugoslavia, based in the Hague, has indicted the Bosnian Serb but has not demanded his extradition, he added.

The prosecution has called more than 20 witnesses who will testify next week during the four-day trial beginning on Monday in the city of Lausanne, to be presided over by a military judge with the rank of lieutenant colonel, Wijnkoop said.

The prosecution's star witness has already identified the defendant. If found guilty, the man could face up to 20 years in prison for torture or a life sentence for murder under the Swiss military penal code, Wijnkoop said.
He said Swiss military justice officials were investigating one more person from former Yugoslavia for alleged war crimes but refused to give details.

The Swiss are also holding a Rwandan, former tea factory head Alfred Musema, in a military prison for alleged crimes during the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis and allied Hutus in the tiny central African country. He has been indicted by the U.N. tribunal investigating the genocide, which sits in Tanzania.
